This game is fun from the get go even if you suck and get stomped at first. The art style and graphics are so deftly crafted and alive, enemies and environments are varied and gorgeously eldritch, seemingly hermetic secrets are a joy to crack, scattered bits of lore are as succulent and alluring as fresh meat nuggets, the music and sound design are immaculate and eerily energizing, and the game play is ceaselessly engaging and heuristic. These merits outshine and render the minor flaws not even worth mentioning. 

You must discover and learn the game yourself, at your own pace. And if you've played Risk of Rain 2, love Returns for what it is and you will enjoy the same splendid hard-earned rewards and laurels 2 offered.

This is essentially a direct upgrade to the original. The new survivor skills are a lot of fun, and have made some of my least favorite survivors from the original a lot more enjoyable to play here. The new survivors themselves are a nice addition, with most of them being pretty strong. 

The updated visuals look beautiful while still retaining the classic Risk of Rain feel. The animated intro and outro is a nice touch. It's a shame that in order to actually see anything or find the teleporter you need to zoom the screen out so much, but even then the game looks good.

Gameplay wise, it's still Risk of Rain. You move slow as balls and your only means of dodging enemies is spamming jump and using whatever mobility skill you may have. With the addition of new alternate skills, navigating the map isn't as bad as it was before. Some survivors have new skills that give them some much needed vertical mobility, or just a general improvement to an already existing horizontal mobility skill. 

The soundtrack still sounds great, all of the tracks have supposedly been remastered, but most of it's pretty subtle. The new tracks sound great, and the existing tracks are just as good as they were before. 

The new gamemode, Providence Trials, is a level-based mode where each Trial has a certain challenge you need to complete in order to unlock a new survivor skill, skin, or item. Some of these are pretty fun, whereas others are really frustrating at times. 

Overall, if you liked the first Risk of Rain, this game is a vast improvement over the original. There's new items, enemies, characters, stage varients, and mechanics that feel right at home with the game. 

If you like Risk of Rain 2 and you're curious about jumping in, just keep in mind that these are two very different games, so just because you're good at Risk of Rain 2 doesn't mean you'll be good at this game right away. It'll take a little bit or even a while.

This game surpasses the modern day standards of what a remaster should be, successfully bringing back the feel of the first game while also feeling like an entirely fresh experience in it of itself. The music, characters (except you artificer), items, maps, replayability, and bosses are just a few of the aspects this game nails perfectly. If you like other risk of rain titles, or just the rogue lite genre in general, this game should be more than worth your time for the low price it asks for.

The main disapproval with the game is the difficulty or frustration with the controls / changes from the original, which I disagree with to a great extent. This game is hard, very hard, and just like any game, learning the controls is one of the first steps to becoming better at a game. The game is very different from most other games out on the market, so it makes sense that the controls are fairly different as well, which even this take is weak with how much rorr gives freedom to customize nearly every single detail of their game, from controls, to the fundamental rules on how levels work, to even ally and enemy damage scaling that is added onto the choice of several difficulties. 

IMO, the people who negatively reviewed the game because of the controls probably came from a different title, thought they could start out with no need to learn the game since they had prior experience, died, then complained about the game rather than realize that this has a completely feel and pattern to it from other games.

I would encourage anyone remotely interested to make the purchase, with the low cost combined with huge replayability potential, and the customization to make the game much easier or harder depending on your skill, allows it to be enjoyed by people from any background or skill.

As a devoted fan of the original Risk of rain, I entered the realm of its remake with a mix of excitement and apprehension. Yet, within minutes of diving into the revamped world, any doubts were swiftly obliterated. This isn't merely a reimagining; it's an exquisite resurrection that surpasses all expectations.

The developers have wielded their magic, transforming every pixel. Each frame is a testament to the dedication poured into resurrecting this classic. From the breathtaking landscapes to the minutest character details, the graphics are a testament to modern gaming prowess.
And the soundtrack! It’s not merely a symphony; it’s an emotional journey. The melodies that once tugged at heartstrings have returned, refined and orchestrated with a finesse that elevates every moment of gameplay.
The gameplay mechanics, oh my, they've transcended. The controls are smooth as silk, offering a seamless experience that bridges the nostalgia of the past with the expectations of the present. Combat feels more engaging, and the overall flow is like a finely tuned masterpiece.
But it's not just about technical prowess; it's about staying faithful to the soul of the original. 
What truly sets this remake apart is its respect for the original while boldly carving its own path.  It's a testament to the dedication of developers who cherish the past while embracing the future.

In summary, this remake isn’t just a game. It’s an experience that doesn’t just surpass the original; it transcends it, setting a new standard for what a remake can achieve. If you have even an ounce of fondness for the original, playing this masterpiece is not just recommended—it's essential.
